text.p: Texaco Inc is looking at different possibilities, including settlement of a race discrimination suit seeking payment of $71 million, spokesman Jim Swords said Monday.

Texaco's stock closed with a gain of 1-1/2 at 97-1/4 Monday after trading as high as 97-3/8 on volume of 1.3 million shares following a report the company is in talks to settle the suit filed in 1994.
The company is "looking at a lot of different possibilities. Settlement is one of them," Swords said when asked about the report.
He declined to go beyond that statement to discuss whether or not there had been any talks.
The Wall Street Journal said Texaco is in formal talks to settle the 1994 race-discrimination suit, citing people familiar with the situation as its sources.

In addition to the talks about the money, the newspaper said, those involved say Texaco is willing to adopt a broader diversity program but wants a third party, rather than plaintiffs' lawyers, to oversee it.
Swords did confirm civil rights leader Jessee Jackson's statment he would be meeting with Texaco officials Tuesday.
